title: Gravity can pull without the two objects touching
summary: Two things do not have to touch for one to exert a force on the other. Gravity pulls with no contact.
body: OpenStax Physics says two bodies do not have to be in physical contact to exert a force. It names gravity as a field force that pulls without contact, and contrasts that with a push you can feel by hand. NASA Glenn's weight guide says the same kind of thing in its own words: gravity is a field force, and the source does not have to touch the object, unlike lift, drag, or thrust. The textbook date is 26 March 2020. The Glenn page was last updated 20 November 2023. Both are general descriptions, not a new experiment.
